articles.title: 8 Potential USMNT Head Coach Replacements for Mauricio Pochettino Amid Manchester United Rumors
articles.summary: Didn't we just talk about this?
articles.body:
The answer is yes, of course . As the World Cup drew to a close four months ago, it was unclear whether U.S. Soccer would try to retain Mauricio Pochettino as its manager for the next cycle, and whether he was interested.

Ultimately, and maybe surprisingly, considering how often Pochettino had already been linked to European jobs, the two sides agreed on a four-year extension. But alas, the charismatic Argentine may fall far short of seeing out that contract.

Credible reporting this week suggests Pochettino is a frontrunner to succeed Michael Carrick at Manchester United. The Red Devils would have to pay a $10 million buyout clause to secure their preferred manager -- and more to bring along his assistants -- but that's not a major sum of money for a club of their stature.

As for us, we're back to wondering again who might be the next full-time USMNT boss if, as seems likely, Pochettino leaves soon.

But four months is a long time in football. In other words, the list needs some updating.

Here are eight potential successors to Pochettino should he find the allure of Old Trafford too great. Four of them were on are original list back in July, and four are newer additions.

Last Managerial Job: Nashville SC (Current)

Why He Makes Sense: Callaghan was a top assistant for USMNT boss Gregg Berhalter during the 2022 cycle, then took over on an interim basis at the start of the next cycle after the end of Berhalter's first contract, and that whole saga with the Reyna family led to an interruption in his tenure.

Those matches under Callaghan went quite well. A full-strength U.S. squad romped through the 2023 Concacaf Nations League semis and finals against Mexico and Canada. A lesser-strength squad played some encouraging football at the 2023 Gold Cup before being eliminated by Panama on penalties.

What's New: At Nashville, Callaghan just guided his charges to an MLS points record and the 2026 Supporters' Shield. In the process, his stock as the American manager of the future may be at an all-time high.

While the MLS Cup Playoffs beckon in November and possibly December, the timing of a potential Pochettino departure now could make a transition for Callaghan easier than if U.S. Soccer had come calling back in the summer.

Last Managerial Job: United States U-23s (Current)

Why He Makes Sense: Cherundolo easily has the most successful managerial resume of former USMNT players from the early 2000s. Most came during a four-year stint at LAFC, where his team won the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup in 2022, and the U.S. Open Cup in 2024.

He also has significant links to the German game, having played his entire pro career at Hannover 96, and has moved back to Germany with his family following the 2025 MLS season. That's arguably an ideal home base for the manager of a national team whose core plays mostly in Europe these days.

What's New: Cherundolo took the U.S. U-23 job with an eye toward the 2028 Olympics shortly before Pochettino's extension was announced. That makes him a likely caretaker manager candidate for the senior squad, even if he's not the long-term choice.

And much of that U-23 squad could be part of the group that competes in the 2030 World Cup. All four of the USMNT starting XIs fielded by Pochettino during the September-October international window averaged 24.0 years old or younger.

Why He Makes Sense : Postecoglou has managed at the highest levels of the European game, winning a UEFA Europa League title with Tottenham Hotspur. Similar to Pochettino, his teams are known for playing an attack-minded style that would be popular with American fans.

Additionally, Postecoglou's formative footballing education came in Australia, a nation similar to the U.S. in terms of where soccer stands in the sports hierarchy. More than most foreign managers, Postecoglou would immediately understand the USMNT's responsibility not only to earn results, but to grow the game.

What's New: Postecoglou started his new job as manager of Saudi giants Al-Nassr over the summer. The Cristiano Ronaldo-led squad currently sits third in the Saudi Pro League table despite earning 2.55 points per match; such is the SPL's top-heavy nature.

We can be pretty certain U.S. Soccer doesn't have Al-Nassr money. But you wonder if the Aussie could be tempted by an exciting new opportunity.

Last Managerial Job: Portugal (Contract expired July 2026)

Why He Makes Sense: For European-born managers, Martínez knows U.S. soccer more than most. He was Tim Howard's manager for the latter portion of his career at Everton, and he's served as a pundit for ESPN, CBS, and others on American TV.

Like Postecoglou, his attack-minded style would also mesh well with U.S. sensibilities, at least more so than the pragmatism of many national team bosses. And his relationship with Cristiano Ronaldo at Portugal suggests that managing any tension involving Christian Pulisic would be child's play by comparison.

What's New: Martínez has stayed mostly out of the headlines since his Portugal tenure ended in a 1-0 loss to eventual World Cup champions Spain in early July. And in hindsight, his decision to lean on Ronaldo in the World Cup looks increasingly unwise.

Yes, there was ugliness between CR7 and the new national team boss, Jorge Jesus, after the latter began diminishing the former's role. But Portugal have won all four of their UEFA Nations League fixtures so far.

Last Managerial Job: Vancouver Whitecaps (present)

Why He Makes Sense: Sørensen has been arguably the most consistent manager in MLS for the last two seasons, despite managing in far from ideal situations in Vancouver, where the team's future is uncertain .

While Sørensen doesn't actually manage in the United States, he's spent two seasons coaching against MLS-based American talent. He also has youth national team management experience, having guided the Denmark U-21 squad from 2021 through 2022.

What's New: After reaching the Concacaf Champions Cup and MLS Cup finals and winning the Canadian Championship final in 2025, 2026 has been a step back in terms of competitive results. Yet Sørensen has arguably performed even better while managing the departures of Sebastian Berhalter, Jayden Nelson and Ali Ahmed.

But after such a ride, the relative stability of national team management could be an appealing new challenge following the 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs, where Vancouver will be a favorite to reach a second consecutive final.

Last Job: Germany (Resigned in July 2021)

Why He Makes Sense: Löw has been out of managing for five years and holds no obvious ties to the U.S. game. But as an assistant, Löw was arguably the brains behind the 2006 German national team that made such an impression on U.S. Soccer that it eventually hired Jürgen Klinsmann to succeed Bob Bradley in 2011.

He's a World Cup winner and two-time medalist. And he should be pretty well-versed in the elite U.S. talent that has found the Bundesliga to be a fruitful European destination over the last decade or so.

What's New: For whatever it's worth, German performances have mostly gotten worse since his departure. Der Mannschaft failed to escape the group stage in the 2022 World Cup and was beaten on penalties by Paraguay in the 2026 round of 32.

Meanwhile, rumors linked Löw to the Ghana national team job, which was eventually taken by Carlos Queiroz, prior to the 2026 World Cup. But similar rumors have come and gone in recent years, and Löw says he could be open to the right national team offer .

Why He Makes Sense: Bradley has the third-most appearances all-time for the USMNT, having suited up 151 times for the Stars and Stripes. He's the son of an American soccer legend in his own right, former USMNT and MLS manager Bob Bradley.

And while he's the least experienced manager on this list, having only recently completed his first season at the senior level, he is exceptionally close to rising USMNT stars Julian Hall and Adri Mehmeti, who were pivotal players for the Red Bulls this year.

What's New: The Red Bulls failed to reach the playoffs for a second consecutive season, marking a first in club history for one of MLS' nine remaining founding members. But few lay the blame at Bradley's feet, given a roster that most agree falls short of current MLS playoff standards.

Why He Makes Sense: I mean, he's Pep freaking Guardiola, one of the most important managers in world football history, not to mention a man who has a well-documented ongoing love of the United States in general and New York City in particular .

And he's still enjoying life outside of managing, serving as an ambassador for City Football Group after finishing out his contract at Manchester City. Maybe he'll be too pricey, or maybe he'll prefer staying in club football, but it never hurts to reach out.

In that context, taking a role like the top job at the USMNT could be particularly appealing. It would allow Guardiola to stay out of the European spotlight if the worst disciplinary consequences come true. And if he transformed the Yanks into a global force to be reckoned with, no one could ever doubt his managerial chops again.

articles.title: Brent Venables' Hot Seat Addressed by Oklahoma's Board of Regents amid 5-4 Record
articles.summary: Despite Oklahoma's 5-4 record this season, the university's board of regents isn't putting pressure on head coach Brent Venables.
articles.body:
Despite Oklahoma's 5-4 record this season, the university's board of regents isn't putting pressure on head coach Brent Venables.

"The board doesn't typically comment much on what's going on in the athletic department. That's maybe a smart thing. But I want to say this … our head coach, Brent Venables, is not on the hot seat," Oklahoma Board of Regents chair Rick Nagel said in a meeting on Wednesday morning, per Joe Mussatto of The Oklahoman .

Venables had led the Sooners to a 10-3 record and a trip to the College Football Playoff last season before losing in the first round. It was the second 10-win season of his tenure since becoming Oklahoma head coach in 2022. He's yet to achieve a postseason win, losing in all three bowl game appearances.

The Sooners bounced back from a 42-25 blowout loss against South Carolina with a 23-7 win over Florida this past Saturday. Oklahoma has failed to string together multiple wins in a row this season, so Venables shook things up by firing offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and promoting Dallas Cowboys legend Jason Witten to offensive play-caller.

"Bragging on his ambition, and his excitement for the opportunity, you can't fabricate that," Venables said of Witten after the win over the Gators. "And I certainly didn't want someone to put a toe in the water, when willing to do it. I wanted someone who saw how good we could be."

Still, with another tough matchup against Ole Miss on deck this week, Oklahoma could revert to its old ways. A poor performance against the Rebels would surely reignite the chatter about Venables' job security.

articles.title: Referee observer Brian Curson gets nine-week ban for discriminatory comments
articles.summary: A Pro Ref referee observer is banned for nine weeks and fined £200 for making discriminatory remarks after a match he was working at.
articles.body:
A Pro Ref referee observer has been suspended for nine weeks and fined £200 for making discriminatory remarks after a match he was working at.

Brian Curson had visited Kenilworth Road to assess the officials at the League One fixture between Luton Town and Rotherham United on 15 November 2025.

An allegation was made that Curson made two discriminatory comments in the lounge at Luton's stadium after the game, which led to the Football Association investigation.

Curson was charged with acting in an improper manner and/or using abusive and/or insulting words.

It was considered an 'aggravated breach', using words which included a reference - whether express or implied - to ethnic origin, race or nationality.

Curson, who has been involved in football for more than 40 years, said that he did not recall making the comments but the FA commission "was satisfied on the balance of probabilities" that they had been made.

The FA requested a time-based sanction because of Curson's role in the sport, as a player would serve a suspension of between nine and 12 matches.

It was determined that, taking into account Curson's experience and role on the day of the match, he should be suspended for nine weeks.

Curson was also told he must attend a mandatory education programme, and received a warning as to future conduct.

articles.title: Scotland: No excuses as Pocognoli seeks first Hampden victory
articles.summary: Having lost his first two home matches, Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli needs to deliver a convincing win against North Macedonia, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
For Sebastien Pocognoli, Friday against North Macedonia is a third opportunity to replace the Hampden Bore with something akin to a Hampden Roar.

Two home games so far under the new head coach and two defeats; five goals conceded, one scored.

The loss to a superior Switzerland was written off because of an early red card for Jack Hendry. The loss to Slovenia had no such mitigation.

Scotland were creatively bereft, physically weak and tactically confused. Captain Andy Robertson said that his team had been out-played and out-fought.

For his own credibility, Pocognoli needs a big night. "Criticism is part of the business as a coach," he says. "It's just about rebounding." This is a huge chance to rebound.

Scotland beat North Macedonia 2-0 in Skopje in his third game in charge. They were without Scott McTominay, Kieran Tierney and Che Adams back then, but they're all in harness now. No excuses, in other words.

Pocognoli insists he learned a few things from that Slovenia game, saying: "We were not intense. We were not aggressive - and this is the one non-negotiable topic with me. We didn't deserve more in that game."

Nations League: Scotland v North Macedonia

Theoretically, Scotland are in better shape now than they were in the last four-game camp.

McTominay is back from his startling heart issues and is scoring again for Napoli. Tierney is one of only a few bright sparks at Celtic. Adams has scored two goals in five games in Italy since he missed the last international window.

There is other encouraging news. Scott Bain's shot-stopping form has to make him a major contender to usurp Angus Gunn in goal. San Jose Earthquakes have conceded eight goals in their last three games. Gunn was badly at fault for one and wasn't too clever for another. Bain has been making the kind of saves that look beyond Gunn.

Luke Graham continues to thrive at centre-back for Stoke City in the English Championship and must be a big option to start. Aaron Hickey has played more football since Slovenia than he did before it.

The same can be said of Ben Gannon-Doak. Before the last camp he had played six times for Bournemouth with an average of 18 minutes per game. Since then, he's played seven with an average of 53 minutes.

He was the man-of-the-match in a 3-0 win against AC Milan. Gannon-Doak must be in a much better place now, physically and mentally.

His club-mate, Ryan Christie, is in a very similar boat. He was more of a substitute than a starter for Bournemouth ahead of the last international break. Lately, he's been one of their go-to guys.

Christie has won eight games in a row with his club and he started in six of those. His confidence must be soaring.

You are Scotland boss Pocognoli - what would you do?

Dalkeith to LA pays off for Porteous with Scotland recall

Turkey-based Bates replaces Binks in Scotland squad

Kieron Bowie is having a difficult time at Sassuolo and Robbie Ure is in-and-out of the Sevilla team, but he scored twice for them last month. Oli McBurnie's painful wait for a Scotland goal carries on, but he has two in his last three for Hull in the Premier League.

Pocognoli says he has no fixed system, no slavish adherence to his favoured back three. It does sound like he's sticking with it for North Macedonia, though.

"I try to find the best shape to make the players shine on the pitch," he says. "After that, it's up to them to show it. But I always try to adapt to my team. I think the shape that we play is the best shape to fit the best quality of the team.

"At Union Saint-Gilloise, when we became champions, we played three at the back because that was the system of the club.

"Sometimes I felt like, if we try a back four, maybe we can have more power in the game, but I didn't do it because the club was building. In Monaco when I make the analysis of the squad, the best shape was a back three, but sometimes we played with a back four.

"It depends on the players' abilities. I believe for this team, right now, it's one of the best shapes. It's a brave style of play that demands a lot of energy. But it's a process. You need to analyse what is good for the future."

Pocognoli feels his team lacked some freshness in the defeat by Slovenia and appears to have some regrets about that, adding: "Maybe we should have rotated a little bit more in the game. That's maybe something that we can reflect on."

What's the big message of the camp so far?

"Continuity and improvement," is the reply. "The main message to the players is try to impress me, try to show that you want to produce something special next season [for the Euros campaign]."

McTominay's presence can only add to Scotland's potential goal threat.

On Tuesday, the Napoli midfielder spoke about his heart issues at the World Cup and his cardiac ablation operation in September.

The fact that he has scored five goals in his past six games for Napoli is testament to not just his ability but his mental and physical strength and his huge desire to kick-on. Pocognoli is thrilled to have him.

"He brings experience," he says. "He's a leader. The age average is quite low in the squad, so it's a massive impact for us to have him back - a player who can pass the message to the young generation and show them direction."

On Friday, that direction needs to be forward with accuracy, speed, aggression and goals.

Whatever formation is deployed against North Macedonia - four defeats out of four with no goals scored and 10 conceded - it needs to deliver an emphatic home win at the third time of asking.

articles.title: Harry Kane: How England captain's 'fairytale' came true as he closes in on appearance record
articles.summary: From 21-year-old who scored 79 seconds into his debut to being on the brink of breaking his nation's appearance record, BBC Sport looks at Harry Kane's England career.
articles.body:
"It's great when fairytales come true," England boss Roy Hodgson said after 21-year-old Tottenham striker Harry Kane scored 79 seconds into his international debut back in 2015.

"Let's hope it's the start of a good and long England career for him."

Eleven years on, Kane will make his 126th appearance for his country and become the most-capped men's player in Three Lions history when England play Croatia in the Nations League at Wembley on Thursday (19:45 GMT).

Peter Shilton, who served England as a goalkeeper, won 125 caps between 1970 and 1990.

"It's not about me - it's about the team," said Kane, scorer of 91 goals in 125 appearances for his country, about his landmark moment.

"I love coming to every England camp, I love playing every game and representing the country in the best way possible."

Kane, 33, has gone through every emotion playing for his country.

He fought back tears after missing a penalty in the World Cup quarter-final defeat by France in 2022, and sang Wonderwall with fans following the win over Croatia at this summer's World Cup - which he labelled one of his "favourite ever moments" in a Three Lions shirt.

London-born Kane is the boy who grew up in Chingford to captain his country, become England's record goalscorer and win the 2026 Ballon d'Or.

Now the Bayern Munich striker stands on the brink of making more appearances than any other man in England's football history.

"He wins the Ballon d'Or, and deservedly so, and in the next game for England he gets the all-time record with 126 matches," England boss Thomas Tuchel said about Kane when announcing his squad last week.

"Thursday is a deserved occasion to celebrate an extraordinary player."

Long before Kane made his first senior appearance for his country in a 4-0 Euro 2015 qualifying win over Lithuania at Wembley, he was an England fan.

Aged 12, he remembers the heartache of going out on penalties to Portugal in the quarter-finals of the 2006 World Cup under Sven-Goran Eriksson and failing to qualify for Euro 2008 under Steve McClaren.

"During most major tournaments we would go to the pub to watch England, with the beer garden and the screen," said Kane.

"We loved England, we loved watching England and we were big England fans. I remember many tears being shed after we went out on penalties and things like that."

Kane fell in love with football from an early age.

Aged five, he wrote about his ambition to become a footballer in a school project.

Weekends and holidays were spent playing football in his local Ridgeway Park with his dad Patrick and brother Charlie.

They would use trees as goalposts, with the two brothers taking turns to shoot while Patrick was in goal.

At Larkswood Primary School, Kane and his friends would play football in the playground - where they were only allowed to use tennis balls.

By then, the future England captain was playing for Sunday league team Ridgeway Rovers - whose former players included David Beckham, Kane's idol growing up.

Former Manchester United midfielder Beckham, who won 115 England caps between 1996 and 2009, was playing for Real Madrid when Kane was at Chingford Foundation School.

"He had sent a Real Madrid shirt back to our secondary school," added Kane.

"Seeing Beckham's shirt hanging there growing up and knowing he grew up in the same surroundings as I did was a source of great motivation."

Wayne Rooney was England captain and Joe Hart was goalkeeper when Kane came on to make his Three Lions debut 11 years ago.

"My reaction when he first came into the England squad was: 'Alright, who is this guy?'" Hart told BBC Sport of the young Tottenham striker called up after scoring 26 goals in 42 league and cup games in 2014-15.

"Then I was like: 'Oh OK, he's good! Then he kept coming back [into the England squad] and my reaction was: 'Flipping heck, he's getting better!'

"I went to Tottenham during Covid and it got to the point in training where he was that good that I wasn't even diving for his shots. I was thinking: 'I adore you, but you are frustrating the life out of me.'"

Kane has served five different England managers.

As well as Hodgson and current boss Tuchel, Kane won 81 of his 125 caps under Gareth Southgate, played for Lee Carsley when he was interim boss in 2024, and appeared in Sam Allardyce's sole match in charge in 2016.

It was Southgate who recognised Kane's leadership skills and handed him the England captaincy for the first time in 2017, even though Kane was not captain of Tottenham at the time.

"I want people with leadership qualities who are respected by the group, and capable of stepping forward at the right moments and handling responsibility," said Southgate.

When he has started, Kane has captained the Three Lions 97 times - more than anyone else.

How long will Kane carry on playing for England? More worryingly, who will lead the attack when he retires?

Despite individual awards and back-to-back Bundesliga titles with Bayern Munich, Kane has yet to inspire his country to a major trophy.

He will be approaching 35 when England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland co-host Euro 2028.

"He aged, but he got better too, like red wine," Lothar Matthaus, West Germany's 1990 World Cup-winning captain, told BBC Sport.

Kane, who has had to adapt his game to stay at the top level, is certainly not ready to talk publicly about retirement dates while he is still only 33.

"From a physical point of view, I feel great," he told BBC Sport recently.

"My numbers are as high as ever, and I've recently reached a new top speed in a game against Borussia Dortmund. I'm going to keep pushing and see what else is possible."

Kane's former Tottenham and England team-mate Hart added: "He's never particularly relied on pace. It's all about his thought process and his brain and how he calculates the game."

The Three Lions have won 83, drawn 22 and lost 20 of the 125 games Kane has appeared in.

His 91 goals for his country include 58 with his right foot, 15 with the left and 18 headers, with three from outside the box. Twenty-six have come from the penalty spot.

Kane's rise from Leyton Orient loan signing to Ballon d'Or winner is well-documented.

His story - the model student and family man who married his childhood sweetheart and became an England great - serves as a reminder to pupils at his old school to never give up on their dreams.

He has not forgotten his roots - or the clubs that helped him on his pathway.

In 2020, Kane sponsored Leyton Orient's shirt. The club's home strip carried a message of thanks to frontline workers tackling the coronavirus pandemic.

Mental health charity Mind and Haven House Children's Hospice also had their logos on Orient's two change shirts as part of the deal.

"I was born and brought up only a couple of miles from Orient's stadium and I'm really happy to have the opportunity to give back to the club that gave me my first professional start," said Kane at the time.

"It also gives me a platform to say a big thank you to the many frontline heroes and charities out there who provide care and support during these challenging times."

Matthaus, who has witnessed Kane's impact at Bayern Munich, added: "He is a good person, a good ambassador, the captain of the English national team playing at a German club."

On Thursday, England's players and fans will salute Kane for breaking another record and making it 126 not out.

articles.title: Copete: "Le lesión acabó convirtiéndose en una pesadilla"
articles.standfirst: El central vuelve a jugar meses después y se desahoga en redes sociales
articles.summary: El central vuelve a jugar meses después y se desahoga en redes sociales
articles.body: Se ha hecho largo... y muy duro. El regreso de Copete a los terrenos de juego se produjo anoche en Mestalla. Un partido intrascendente de Copa poco rentable deportivamente, pero un paso de gigante para el central llegado del Mallorca. Muchos meses después el zurdo ha superado un calvario y ya puedo volver a disfrutar de su profesión. Han pasado muchas cosas con problemas con el cuerpo médico de por medio, pero ahora la clave es que ya está listo para jugar e ir creciendo en un Valencia que le ha echado de menos. El jugador eligió las redes sociales para escribir sus sentimientos tras el partido ante el Tavernes. "Han sido meses muy difíciles a nivel profesional y, seguramente, también algunos de los más complicados de mi vida en lo personal. Me ha tocado enfrentarme a una lesión que acabó convirtiéndose en una pesadilla y en un reto que jamás imaginé que tendría que afrontar. Un proceso que he sufrido cada día, pero en el que también he puesto todo de mi parte para conseguir volver. Ha habido momentos especialmente complicados, días de dudas y situaciones difíciles de explicar en unas pocas líneas. Pero incluso en esos momentos tenía claro que iba a hacer todo lo posible por salir adelante y volver a estar aquí", asegura el central en su escrito. "He tenido a mi gente cerca durante todo este tiempo, acompañándome y viviendo este proceso conmigo. Gracias de corazón a cada persona que ha estado a mi lado, me ha apoyado y me ha dado fuerzas durante estos meses. Hoy, por fin, puedo decir que estoy de vuelta. Orgulloso del esfuerzo, la paciencia y todo el trabajo que ha habido detrás para llegar hasta aquí. Ahora toca seguir trabajando, disfrutar de volver a hacer lo que más me gusta y ayudar al equipo a conseguir nuestros objetivos", comentaba en su publicación a la que respondieron varios compañeros de equipo felicitándose por su regreso y deseando que Diego López y Canós, los únicos que faltan por abandonar la enfermería, lo hagan cuanto antes.

articles.title: De la Fuente: "Lamine tenía líquido en la rodilla, a ver si se enteran, ¿ha quedado claro?"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del seleccionador español
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente ha pasado por la sala de prensa del estadio del Sparta de Praga para analizar el partido ante los checos. Su primer mensaje ha sido un directo a la mandíbula de quienes han puesto en duda las molestias de Lamine Yamal en la rodilla derecha. Lamine y Oyarzabal: "Hablar desde el desconocimiento en la vida es triste, lamentable. Por eso vengo a dar luz. Lamine tiene inflamación en la rodilla. Nuestro servicio médico lo vio y yo decidí que, para evitar este viaje, preferí que se quedara en su casa entrenando con el club. Y de igual manera, Mikel Oyarzabal". Zubimendi: "Es el segundo mejor jugador del mundo en esa posición después de Rodri. Nos aporta muchísimo. No me inquietan las ausencias. Todos son muy buenos". Más de Lamine: "Hablé ayer y hoy con él. Igual que con Mikel. La evolución es buena. La recuperación es buena y creemos que el viernes va a estar con nosotros". ¿Lamine tiene privilegios?: "No me preocupan los mensajes de fuera porque ya estoy yo para aclararlo. La gente crea argumentos que no tienen que ver con la realidad. Lamine no tiene ningún privilegio. Esto lo hubiéramos hecho por cualquier otro jugador". Mikel Merino: "Mikel es un jugador ambicioso, consciente de su talento y categoría. Podía jugar aquí y en cualquier selección del mundo. Pero todos los compañeros tienen ese nivel. En mi análisis, el futbolista que sale aprovechándose del trabajo de un compañero es el más importante. Para nosotros son todos muy importantes. Y Mikel tiene un peso específico en este equipo". Más de Zubimendi: "Nosotros tratamos a todos por igual. Muchos me decís que hay jugadores que juegan mejor en la selección que en su club. Y Martín es ese tipo. Entiende perfectamente su papel. Cuando juega, cuando no juega... Es una suerte tener este tipo de futbolistas con nosotros". La racha de España: "Buscas muchas motivaciones. Esa es una muy evidente, muy clara. Queremos seguir marcando hitos. Queremos seguir creciendo. Lo más importante es la autoexigencia". El once y la portería: "Si digo que sí, lo dejo claro. Y si digo que no, también. Tenemos cuatro porterazos y cualquiera de los que pongamos lo va a hacer bien. Yo no conocía personalmente a Álvaro Valles y encaja perfectamente con nuestra mentalidad y filosofía" ¿Condiciona Inglaterra la alineación?: "No, porque queremos ganar mañana. Sólo existe mañana". Más de la portería, Unai: "Es el mejor portero del mundo, la mejor persona del mundo y el mejor capitán del mundo. Da gusto convivir con él. Ha evolucionado, ha cambiado futbolísticamente... En lo humano ya sabíamos que era una gran persona. Es una suerte tener a este tipo de futbolistas". ¿Especialmente enfadado con Lamine?: "Lo que más me duele es la mentira, la falta de rigor, la falta de veracidad y el invento. Es por lo que he contado más cosas de las que debiera, pero es la única manera de que la gente sepa cuál es la realidad. No aguanto a la gente que trata de engañarte y mentir". Santi Denia: "Somos amigos y me alegro de todo lo bueno que le pase. He aprendido mucho de Santi Denia. Él me enseñó a ser seleccionador. Hará un gran trabajo aquí". Dani Olmo y quién jugará con el 10: "Va evolucionando bien. Los dorsales los eligen los jugadores por veteranía... No sé quién lo va a coger".

articles.title: Breno Sales hails Brazil U17s' collective strength ahead of World Cup
articles.summary: Breno Sales in action for Brazil U-17Credits: Fabio Souza /CBFWinning the U-17 World Cup and bringing the trophy home to Brazil: that is the goal for Breno S...
articles.body:
Breno Sales in action for Brazil U-17 Credits: Fabio Souza /CBF

Winning the U-17 World Cup and bringing the trophy home to Brazil: that is the goal for Breno Sales and the other players called up by coach Carlos Eduardo Patetuci. The Vasco centre-back sees individual quality, intensity and team spirit as some of Brazil's main strengths heading into the tournament, which will be held in Qatar.

"We have just one goal: to become champions and bring this World Cup home to Brazil. God willing, we'll have a good tournament and come out on top," he said.

Breno believes that the ability to win individual duels, combined with the determination to win possession and total commitment during matches, could make the difference in Brazil's campaign.

Breno Sales, Brazil U-17 centre-back Credits: Fabio Souza /CBF

"We have individual skill, quality in one-on-one situations, determination and unity. We run all the time, we never stop running, and we're always looking to win possession and keep the ball," he explained.

Another factor the defender considers important is the experience shared within the squad. Having players who have already had opportunities in professional football allows for an exchange of knowledge that, he says, helps the whole group mature.

"It's important to seek their advice and listen to what they have to say. It's an exchange. We learn from them and also try to help a little," he explained.

Born in 2009, Breno also values the bonds built over successive call-ups. The centre-back believes that understanding one another helps the team cope with pressure and gives the players greater confidence on the pitch.

"We always try to help each other, regardless of the moment or the circumstances. That makes things easier, because it takes some of the pressure out of the game. It also reduces the fear of making mistakes, since we're all together, supporting each other," he said.

Being called up for the World Cup marks a special achievement in the player's career. Breno celebrated the news with his family and highlighted what it means to represent his country in a competition of this magnitude.

"Every child who plays football dreams of having the chance to play in an U-17 World Cup. I celebrated with my family. It was a dream and, thank God, I'm getting to fulfil it. Wearing the Brazil shirt is something that really touches my heart," he revealed.

Brazil are in Group I of the U-17 World Cup alongside Ireland, Tanzania and Costa Rica. The team will make their debut on November 21 against Ireland.

articles.title: Brad Friedel: Shrewsbury Town 'hit all the boxes' for new owners
articles.summary: In an exclusive interview with BBC Radio Shropshire new Shrewsbury Town sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is a perfect fit for the new owners.
articles.body:
Shrewsbury Town's new sporting director Brad Friedel says the club is the perfect project for the US-backed owners after a Europe-wide search ended with them taking contol of the League Two outfit.

Scott Davidson's Biscayne ST LLC consortium, which Friedel is part of, completed their takeover on Monday, buying 87.4% of the shares and allowing long-time owner Roland Wycherley to relinquish control.

"Scott and I met through friends in Miami and through the love of football and nothing more or less," former Blackburn and USA goalkeeper Friedel told BBC Radio Shropshire in an exclusive interview.

"As we got to know each other, our thoughts on business and football aligned - we got to the point where we said let's try to find a club which fits a whole bunch of criteria.

"So we looked in Turkey, Poland, Portugal and Holland but the clubs we were looking at, something didn't align for one reason or another and a lot of it came down to did we think our group can help the football club because we want to bring the town firmly behind the club."

Wycherley first announced his plans to find a successor five years ago and Friedel says with Davidson already being a majority shareholder of Edinburgh-based The Spartans in Scottish League Two, they wanted a club they could take forward both on and off the field.

"The one-town club really appealed to us because we want to intergrate the club even more into the town than it is now and when you look at the investment going into the EFL, the foreign investment going into it, there's a reason for it because there's no better place for football than the United Kingdom.

"Once we decided our group would be best suited to the UK market, Shrewsbury hit all the boxes of what we like, but also what we feel we can deliver towards the club and the town."

Shrewsbury takeover in 'final stages' - Wycherley

Friedel group completes Shrewsbury Town takeover

As a player, Friedel spent the majority of his career in the Premier League with Liverpool, Blackburn, Aston Villa and Tottenham, but the 55-year-old is unfazed about taking his first sporting director role in England's fourth tier.

"I don't look at football anymore as I would only take a job in the Premier League or the Champions League," he said. "One of my most enjoyable jobs post-playing career was being head coach of the US men's under-19 national team and most of those players weren't even professional.

"I look at football opportunities with different projects. The upside if you get it right in English football is there is such a buzz for me out of it, so I don't look at this as an EFL League Two club, I look at is as another incredible project with incredible people."

Shrewsbury finished 10 points clear of relegation in League Two last season, appointing current boss and former player, Gavin Cowan in January to help steer them clear of a drop into the National League and Friedel intends to work closely with the head coach.

"I'm moving over here, I'll be there day-to-day so this is not a situation where you'll see me every now and then at the club, I'm not here for the short term," he added.

"It'll be a collaboration - the way we see football being successful is you have to have roles and structure but you can't have dictators, so Gavin and I will be around each other every day, I'll be at training every day.

"It's a group effort. If we're successful it will have nothing to do with just what I do or Scott does or Gavin does, it's everybody on the field and off the field who has to pull their weight for us to be successful."

One area the new owners intend to concentrate on is recruitment with Friedel revealing a department is already at work identifying potential new signings.

"I'm very much data driven but I'd never sign a player just on data as there are so many different elements to signing a player," he said.

"What data does is speed up the process and we have our own customised platform and we'll be bringing in other individuals to help with the recruitment process and we'll collaborate with Gavin and extend a much wider net around the globe looking for players.

"We will reach out to many parts of the world that have not been previously by Shrewsbury Town - we're excited about bringing this recruitment department in and it's something that's already in place and they're here and we're already working."

The current campaign is Shrewsbury's second in League Two after a 10-season stay in League One ended in 2025 while they last played in the second tier in 1989 but Friedel is not ruling out the club returning to that level at some point in the future.

"Everything is possible, you've got to dream but let's take one thing at a time - we want to come in and take this step-by-step," he added.

"We want to be possible promotion contenders whether it's this season or next season, that's what our aim is and if we're fortunate enough to get up into League One we'll try to do it again and if we get up into the Championship that's another formidable task.

"We want to baby-step this a little bit, first stability, structure and make sure we're providing the resources needed for the first-team staff, for the players to be successful and for the academy to be successful and then see where we go."

articles.title: Marcus Rashford races to be fit for Liverpool trip as Man Utd put new recovery programme in place for his groin problem
articles.summary: Manchester United are hopeful Marcus Rashford will be fit for their trip to Liverpool a week on Sunday after the forward began a new treatment programme on a...
articles.body:
Manchester United are hopeful Marcus Rashford will be fit for their trip to Liverpool a week on Sunday after the forward began a new treatment programme on a groin problem. The 29-year-old has missed United's last six games, but a visit to a specialist in Dublin has given the club fresh optimism ahead of a clash against the rivals he has so often hurt.

Manchester United hope Rashford will be available for their next game at Liverpool a week on Sunday after he started a new recovery programme, according to the Daily Mail . The forward travelled to Dublin last week with a member of the club's medical staff to see a groin specialist, and a fresh plan is now in place.

Rashford picked up a hip injury at the World Cup before returning to Old Trafford in the summer following a season on loan at Barcelona. He has since missed United's last six games after the problem was aggravated and spread to his groin.

Rashford offered to play through the pain

Rashford featured in the first six league games of the season, as well as the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton and the Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid in mid-October. He is said to have a good relationship with Michael Carrick and wanted to support the head coach during a difficult spell.

However, playing while carrying the injury only made it worse. It is understood Rashford even offered to go on the bench for last month's defeat at Chelsea, but United decided it was not worth the risk of further damage.

Rashford is yet to score for United since his return from Barcelona, but his record against Liverpool offers real cause for optimism. The England international has scored seven goals in 20 appearances against United's biggest rivals, which makes him a valuable option for the trip to Anfield.

He will continue to work his way back to fitness during the international break, with United hopeful he will be ready for the game on November 22. His return would be a timely lift for a squad that has been missing one of its most experienced attackers.

What comes next for Rashford and United?

The Liverpool clash could also mark the start of a new era at Old Trafford. The report adds that Carrick is expected to be sacked and replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, which means the trip to Anfield could be his first game in charge.

Pochettino would be returning to the Premier League after previous spells at Tottenham, Chelsea and Southampton.

articles.title: No. 6 Indiana is hoping another stingy defense can slow down No. 15 USC's high-scoring offense
articles.summary: Indiana coach Curt Cignetti always invests heavily in a strong defense.It paid off before he took the Hoosiers job, during his first two seasons in Bloomingt...
articles.body:
Indiana coach Curt Cignetti always invests heavily in a strong defense.

It paid off before he took the Hoosiers job, during his first two seasons in Bloomington, and it's proved to be even more valuable more this year with Indiana's offense bogged down as starting quarterback Josh Hoover battles a right arm injury.

They'll need to deliver again Saturday, too, when No. 6 Indiana hosts No. 15 USC in what amounts to an elimination game to make the final Big Ten championship. The Hoosiers (8-1, 5-1 Big Ten, No. 9 CFP) insist they're up for the challenge.

"As long as there's still time on the clock, we're still in it," seventh-year defensive back Preston Zachman said. "We're going to keep swinging. We're going to keep fighting, and we're going to keep fighting and swinging and see what happens at the end."

That's exactly why Indiana still is in the playoff chase despite failing to score more than 23 points in four straight games. And while the names and faces have changed throughout Cignetti's tenure, the constant has been a virtually impenetrable defense.

In 2024, Indiana finished sixth in the Football Bowl Subdivision in scoring defense (15.6 points). Last year, the Hoosiers were second (11.7). This year, the unit is fourth (12.44).

Indiana ranks fourth in run defense (75.6 yards), fifth in total defense (259.2) and sacks per game (3.56), 19th in third-down conversion percentage allowed (31.6%) and 24th in pass defense (183.7 yards). Opponents have only seven TDs through nine games, too.

But the one missing element has been takeaways. Indiana has only nine, and that's something they'd like to change during these final three regular-season games and what they hope lurks beyond them.

Southern California coach Lincoln Riley knows just how tough it will be even with an extra week to prepare.

"They've had a really strong year defensively," Riley said. "I think they're led by their defensive front. It's a very deep, very talented front. Probably in terms of the number of quality bodies they put out there, it's probably one of the deepest groups we've played all year. They create a lot of havoc, and they do a nice job in coverage."

It starts with Tobi Osunsanmi, who is having a career season. In four years at Kansas State, the 6-foot-2, 250-pound defensive end had 49 tackles and 8 1/2 sacks. This year, he leads Indiana's front four with 34 tackles while ranking third nationally with 10 sacks and has recorded at least one in eight straight games.

Osunsanmi has made such a big impact, he's now one of 12 semifinalists for the prestigious Lombardi Award — putting him in position to become the first Hoosier to be honored as college football's top offensive or defensive linemen or linebacker. And the secret to his success is simple.

"Effort, I feel like a lot of sacks come off of effort," he said after Indiana's victory at Michigan. "I feel like our whole defense really, we just hunt every play. We hunt. We know that if we're sending pressure, it's expected to hit. If the defensive line is rushing, we're expected to cause havoc. That's what we're here to do, cause havoc."

The Trojans (7-2, 4-2, No. 18) tossed out the student body right philosophy years ago and is now relying on a pass heavy offense. The result: USC has matched Indiana's scoring average (32.4 points), is 12th nationally in passing (294.4) while 129th in rushing (129.3).

Cignetti knows this game could come down to two things — winning the third-down battle and whether the Trojans can protect quarterback Jayden Maiava. Cignetti calls him smart, accurate and quick and believes he'll play in the NFL when his college days end.

Just don't bet against this well-rested defense following a bye week.

"We've got to limit the explosive (plays)," Zachman said. "I mean we've got to get after him (Maiava). We've got to pressure him, kind of get him out of the pocket and make him uncomfortable."

articles.title: Mikel Merino: "¿Mi rol? Que mi padre haya sido entrenador me hace ver el fútbol de otra manera"
articles.standfirst: Rueda de prensa del centrocampista de la selección española
articles.summary: Rueda de prensa del centrocampista de la selección española
articles.body: Después de la rueda de prensa de Luis de la Fuente, fue Mikel Merino quien compareció ante los medios en la sala de prensa del Sparta de Praga para trasladar la visión del vestuario de la selección española en la víspera del partido frente a la República Checa de Santi Denia. Mikel Merino sobre ser titular: "Por supuesto. ¿A qué jugador no le gustaría tener más minutos? Si hay alguien que tiene la suerte de tener este entrenador soy yo. A mí nunca me escucharás quejarme de la decisión de un entrenador, pero lo que quiero es jugar". Posible salida del Arsenal para él o Zubimendi: "No sentirse en el césped la mayor parte del tiempo no es lo ideal para un jugador. El Arsenal es el mejor equipo del mundo actualmente y es muy difícil contar con minutos. Ahora sabemos qué rol nos toca y los dos estamos tranquilos y con ganas de seguir entrenando a tope para demostrar que podemos seguir estando ahí". Más sobre jugar poco: "No sólo puedes valer para un contexto. Hay que hacer el trabajo que toca cuando toca. Que me den la enhorabuena por mi trabajo siempre es positivo". Los récords: "No hemos hablado nada de ello. Sabemos que es importante y está ahí, pero nuestro único objetivo es el siguiente partido". Su rol en el equipo: "Es difícil interiorizar eso. Somos egoístas en muchos casos y vemos el fútbol desde un prisma individual. Pero que mi padre haya sido entrenador me hace ver el fútbol de otra manera. Los que terminan los partidos son los que ganan los campeonatos. Es difícil convencernos muchas veces". Barrenetxea: "No he hablado con él, pero le mando todo el ánimo del mundo. Es difícil perderse concentraciones como esta". Praga dos veces en una semana: "Es gente muy trabajadora y que no se rinde. No esperamos un partido fácil y tendremos que dar nuestra mejor versión para ganar". Santi Denia: "Es alguien con el que he tenido muchas conversaciones. Está intentando traer el modelo español a la selección checa. Es muy inteligente, trabaja mucho y se adapta muy bien. Él y Pablo Amo obtendrán buenos resultados". Los jóvenes y las novatadas: "Se han adaptado muy bien. El grupo humano es espectacular y todos son bienvenidos. Alguno tendrá que cantar o bailar más adelante por la novatada".

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel committed to England until Euro 2028 but keen on club return in future
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel is committed to England until Euro 2028 - even if a big club comes calling - but does hope to return to the club game after leaving the Three Lions; Tuchel reveals he does not have a release clause in his current England contract
articles.body:
The Three Lions boss was asked the question amid Mauricio Pochettino agreeing a deal in principle with Manchester United to replace Michael Carrick, who is expected to be sacked in the coming days. The USA manager has a £7m buyout clause in his deal.

"No release clause," confirmed Tuchel, who signed his current contract in February. "And there's no intention. I signed the contract - I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business."

Tuchel was then asked if there was "zero chance" he would leave England if a big club came in for him between now and the 2028 Euros, which will be hosted in England. The manager said: "Yeah, I would say so."

Tuchel led England to the semi-finals at this summer's World Cup in the USA, where they were beaten in heartbreaking fashion by Argentina.

His side have won three of four Nations League matches since the World Cup - including a 7-0 win in Croatia - and Tuchel said: "I love my group of players, I love my staff and I have bosses who trust me and are happy with the way we do things.

"It's a lot and I know how to appreciate it a lot, so it's in a good place. I'm in a good place. Like I said, I love the players.

"I miss my players and I miss my team and I miss the 50 matches that I'm not involved in a year, but I'm desperate to win the Nations League and I'm desperate to play and try to win the Euros."

Despite enjoying his first role in international football, Tuchel - who has coached Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain - admits he intends to return to club football once he departs his current role.

"Yeah, definitely. I miss the 50 matches, like I said. I miss these two minutes when everything is done. You go out the two minutes before the whistle goes, it's like the best two minutes, everything is done and you're in a full stadium, lights are on and you're just so excited and you're part of it.

"That's actually the two minutes where I kind of a little bit realise how lucky and how grateful I am, and then the whistle goes and you're just in the tunnel again and you're trying to win the game for your team. And you do that every four days."

Could Nations League finals come to England?

Tuchel also suggested the FA could make a bid to bring the Nations League finals to England - something he hopes will happen.

He said: "We don't know where the final of the Nations League will be yet. The FA has an option to put their hat in the ring.

"We've talked before about this group of players struggling to bring their training performances to the field. Other England managers have spoken about the shirt being heavy.

"It's [the Euros] going to be a home tournament, the pressures of that tournament will be unique. It's almost like a dress rehearsal, playing in front of your own fans.

"Nations League helps in general for us. It would be exciting, it would be nice to have it here. First of all, we need to reach the final."

England are currently second in Group C, three points behind leaders Spain and six ahead of third-placed Croatia - meaning they are well-placed to reach the finals next summer.

articles.title: La selección española estrena 'fichajes' de cuatro ruedas: EBRO de siete plazas y etiqueta CERO
articles.standfirst: Luis de la Fuente y Sonia Bermúdez han participado en la entrega de una flota de EBRO s800 y s900 híbridos enchufables a la RFEF, con hasta 140 kilómetros de autonomía eléctrica.
articles.summary: Luis de la Fuente y Sonia Bermúdez han participado en la entrega de una flota de EBRO s800 y s900 híbridos enchufables a la RFEF, con hasta 140 kilómetros de autonomía eléctrica.
articles.body: La selección española de fútbol tiene nuevos 'fichajes'. Aunque esta vez no han sido Luis de la Fuente ni Sonia Bermúdez quienes han elegido a los nuevos integrantes de la familia de la Federación Española de Fútbol, sino que llegan directamente desde una marca automovilística española, EBRO, que ha entregado en la Ciudad del Fútbol de Las Rozas una flota de sus SUV híbridos enchufables s800 y s900. Se trata de los dos modelos tope de la gama EBRO, ambos con un interior de siete plazas, etiqueta CERO y hasta 140 kilómetros de autonomía eléctrica, más que suficiente para los recorridos diarios. Los nuevos vehículos ya están a disposición del personal de la Federación y, a partir de ahora, darán servicio a la actividad deportiva e institucional de la RFEF. La marca española ofrece a la Federación sus dos modelos más grandes, lujosos y capaces. Empezando por el EBRO s800, un SUV de 4,7 metros (segmento D) que, en su versión híbrida enchufable entrega 279 CV de potencia. Su batería de 18,3 kWh permite recorrer 90 kilómetros con energía eléctrica con cada recarga. El escalón superior, el s900, se va a los 4,81 metros (como el s800, su configuración es de siete plazas 2+3+2), pero su mecánica es notablemente más capaz. Ofrece nada menos que 428 caballos y un alcance de 140 kilómetros con cada recarga de electricidad. Sus precios, teniendo en cuenta lo que ofrecen, son bastante competitivos. El EBRO s800 PHEV cuesta en España 31.900 euros (esta tarifa incluye las ayudas del Plan Auto+ y todos los descuentos que ofrece actualmente la marca), mientras que el s900 se va los 41.590 euros, también financiado y con todas las rebajas posibles. Aunque, como es lógico, la selección campeona del mundo (tanto masculina como femenina) es un icono insuperable, la vinculación de EBRO con el fútbol patrio no se limita solo al equipo nacional. La marca con sede en Barcelona también se ha convertido esta temporada en patrocinador de las competiciones nacionales que organiza la Real Federación Española de Fútbol, esto es la Copa de SM el Rey, la Copa de la Reina y la Supercopa de España

articles.title: Kamario Taylor Becomes Highest-Paid QB in CFB, Latest Rumors on New Mississippi State Contract
articles.summary: Mississippi State sophomore quarterback Kamario Taylor likely would've been the most coveted player in the transfer portal this offseason, but he reportedly won't be going anywhere.
articles.body:
Mississippi State sophomore quarterback Kamario Taylor likely would've been the most coveted player in the transfer portal this offseason, but he reportedly won't be going anywhere.

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported that Taylor is finalizing a deal to return to Mississippi State in 2027. Pete Nakos and Chris Low of On3.com reported that the deal is worth $7.5 million and could rise to $9 million with incentives, making him the highest-paid quarterback in all of college football.

Mississippi State and Taylor confirmed he will return:

Thamel added that the timing of Taylor's new deal will allow Bulldogs head coach Jeff Lebby to "build a recruiting/portal class around Taylor, as the school pitched Taylor on an uptick in overall investment."

"One of the things we realized is the level of quality players who are intrigued by joining Kamario at Mississippi State," a source told Thamel.

Taylor played in six games this season and led the Bulldogs (4-5) to a 4-0 start, throwing for 1,460 yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions. It was announced last month that he needed to undergo season-ending surgery on a toe injury, cutting his breakout campaign short.

"Over the last few weeks, I've worked every day with our medical staff and done everything possible to be out there with my teammates," Taylor said in a statement at the time. "Missing the rest of this season is hard to accept, but I know God has a plan. … My role will look different these next few weeks, but my commitment to this team won't change. I'll do whatever I can to help my brothers down the stretch."

Taylor's presence could help Mississippi State enter the national spotlight in 2027, as more talented players could be on the way to help lead the team to College Football Playoff contention.

articles.summary: Manu Hernando y Álvaro Fernández firmaron la remontada del equipo cántabro
articles.body: El Racing ganó 1-2 al Al Madina en Trípoli(Libia) en un amistoso donde José Alberto apostó por los futbolistas menos habituales. Se adelantó el conjunto libio de penalti en el minuto 22. En el minuto 34, Manu Hernando de cabeza a la salida de un córner, empataba el partido para llegar con igualada al descanso. En el tramo final del partido, Álvaro Fernández establecía el definitivo 1-2. Para este choque José Alberto no pudo contar con los lesionados Mantilla, Andrés Martín, Aguirrezabala y Maguette, además de Zabiri, Guliashvili, Pablo y Belocian que se encuentran con sus respectivas selecciones. Lo más positivo fue el primer partido disputado por Eriksson después de superar su lesión de hombro. El meta sueco se lesionó prácticamente al inicio de temporada. Álvaro Mantilla, por otra parte, fue operado con éxito de la rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior de la rodilla derecha que se produjo en el partido disputado ante el Real Madrid en los Campos de Sport. La intervención quirúrgica fue realizada en el hospital Santa Clotilde situado en Santander. El Doctor Cruz, encargado de realizar la intervención, practicó a Mantilla una reconstrucción del ligamento dañado con una plastia procedente del tendón rotuliano. El periodo de baja del lateral cántabro, que ya ha recibido el alta hospitalaria, dependerá de la evolución de su lesión.

articles.title: Estalla el caso Lamine: "Me duele la mentira, la falta de rigor y el invento"
articles.standfirst: Luis de la Fuente salió en defensa del crack de la selección.
articles.summary: Luis de la Fuente salió en defensa del crack de la selección.
articles.body: La ausencia de Lamine Yamal en en el compromiso de la selección española en Praga despertó todo tipo de especulaciones. La RFEF comunicó de forma oficial que el extremo había sentido molestias en la rodilla derecha tras el partido contra el Atlético de Madrid y que, por ese motivo, no estaría en el partido frente a la República Checa, ya que continuaría su proceso de recuperación en Barcelona. Tanto él como Mikel Oyarzabal, con otro tipo de dolencias, se perderían en primer partido, pero no necesariamente el segundo que se juega el domingo en el Metropolitano frente a Inglaterra. La ausencia de Mikel no fue cuestionada mediáticamente, pero la de Lamine sí que despertó todo tipo de especulaciones. Aparecieron informaciones que apuntaban a que el jugador "se borraba" del primer encuentro y eso es algo que ha molestado mucho a Luis de la Fuente, que ha sido más contundente que nunca: "Lo que más me duele es la mentira, la falta de rigor, la falta de veracidad y el invento. Lo he contado todo todo porque es la única manera de que la gente sepa cuál es la realidad. No aguanto a la gente que trata de engañar y mentir", respondió a MARCA. El contacto entre los servicios médicos de la selección y el Barcelona es constante, así que ambas partes pactaron los pasos a seguir en consenso con el jugador y con Luis de la Fuente. "Lamine tiene inflamación en la rodilla. Nuestro servicio médico lo vio y yo decidí que, para evitar este viaje, preferí que se quedara en su casa y entrenando con el club. Hablar desde el desconocimiento en la vida es triste, lamentable. Por eso vengo a dar luz", aseguró el seleccionador. En definitiva, fue Luis de la Fuente el que, basándose en los informes médicos, no ha querido tomar riesgos con Lamine y, como hace habitualmente con el resto de jugadores, prefiere no contar con él en un encuentro y evitar así un riesgo importante de una lesión mayor. La decisión tomada con Lamine no tiene nada que ver con su estatus dentro del grupo. Es obvio que se trata de un jugador diferencial, pero no recibe un trato excepcional. Y aquí el debate externo no afecta. El grupo es sólido y sabe que no hay diferencias ni tratos de favor. "No me preocupan los mensajes de fuera porque ya estoy yo para aclararlo. La gente crea argumentos que no tienen que ver con la realidad. Lamine no tiene ningún privilegio. Esto lo hubiéramos hecho por cualquier otro jugador", admitió Luis de la Fuente.

articles.title: Premier League Darts: Matt Porter backs 'solid' format but hints at 'fresh concepts' as Ross Smith enters the conversation
articles.summary: PDC chief executive Matt Porter speaks exclusively to Sky Sports, touching on potential Premier League Darts format changes, Ross Smith and Michael van Gerwen; Sky Sports remains home of darts with Grand Slam of Darts (Nov 14-22), World Darts Championship (Dec 11-Jan 3)
articles.body:
Speaking to Sky Sports on Wednesday, Porter touched on whether changes are coming to the Premier League, and also whether Ross Smith may be included and Michael van Gerwen may miss out on the tournament in 2027.

Premier League Darts, broadcast exclusively live on Sky Sports , has undergone several format changes since its launch in 2005. The most recent revamp, introduced in 2022, saw the competition reduced to eight players, with a nightly winner crowned at each weekly event.

Under the current format, each of the 16 regular league nights features a mini-tournament, consisting of quarter-finals, semi-finals and a final, giving players the chance to collect valuable points and secure a nightly victory.

Each nightly winner is awarded five points, while the runner-up collects three. The two losing semi-finalists receive two points apiece, with the four players beaten in the quarter-finals earning no points.

The previous format, last used in 2021, featured 10 players competing in a round-robin league. Each player contested one best-of-12-leg match per night, with the bottom two in the standings eliminated following the ninth week of action, famously known as 'Judgement Night'.

The remaining eight players then continued in the round-robin format for a further seven weeks, before the top four progressed to the play-offs - a stage of the competition that remains unchanged under the current format.

"I think the format is solid," Porter said. "I think the fact you see the top players playing each other every week is strong.

"It's great for the live crowds in the arenas. It keeps them engaged. It keeps fans on TV engaged until the end.

"Previously, when there'd been just more generic league stage matches, you'd see a fall off in attendance and you'd see people leaving the arenas as the evening went on, and that's not something we want.

"But we're very conscious of the need to keep it fresh. The Premier League format has evolved a number of times over its 20-odd year history, and it will continue to do so.

"So we've got a couple of little concepts that we're looking at and things we'll introduce at the right time.

"We'll never keep everybody happy, but as long as they're talking about it, that's all we can ask for."

'Smith now one of the best players in the world'

Speaking recently, Smith said he believes he 'definitely' deserves a Premier League debut on current form , having secured a second TV major title of the season at the Machineseeker European Championship.

Smith joined Van Gerwen, Phil Taylor, Rob Cross and Peter Wright as a multiple winner of the European Championship, following his 2022 success by defeating Martin Schindler 11-8 in the final in Dortmund on Sunday.

The Englishman's latest triumph adds to his World Series Finals victory in September and sees him rise to a career-high sixth in the PDC Order of Merit. He has also enjoyed an impressive season on the European Tour and Players Championship circuit, claiming two titles in each competition.

For the Premier League, the top four players in the PDC Order of Merit following the conclusion of the World Darts Championship will automatically qualify, with four additional wildcard selections completing the eight-player line-up for the 16-week regular season

"Ross [Smith] has had a magnificent year," Porter said.

"He won the European Championship a few years ago, but perhaps at the time didn't then back that up by getting into the latter stages of tournaments on a regular basis.

"He's proven now that he can do that. He's proven he can live with and beat the best players in the world.

"And he now is one of the best players in the world. So I don't think it would be a surprise for many people if Ross were to be included."

Van Gerwen, a seven-time Premier League champion (2013, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2022 and 2023), has endured one of the most challenging seasons of his career.

The 37-year-old has progressed beyond the opening round in just one of his last five tournaments, reaching the quarter-finals of Players Championship 30 before suffering defeat to Scott Williams.

That loss further underlined Van Gerwen's struggles this season, having suffered first-round exits at four European Tour events: the European Darts Trophy, German Darts Grand Prix, Flanders Darts Trophy and Swiss Darts Trophy. It is his highest number of opening-round defeats in a single season since the European Tour began in 2012.

Van Gerwen also lost in the first round at the World Grand Prix and European Championship this year, losing in the second round of the World Matchplay.

On rumours Van Gerwen could miss out on the Premier League, Porter said: "I think Michael's career record speaks for itself.

"He's had a difficult year, but, you know, he's committed to the tour.

"He's stuck by what he wants to do, and I think he'll come again."

articles.title: Longtime NFL QB and former NC State QB Philip Rivers reportedly set to be Wolfpack's new head coach
articles.summary: Rivers had been negotiating with NC State since at least Sunday.
articles.body:
After multiple days of negotiations , Philip Rivers is set to be NC State's new coach.

Per On3, the school will hire the former Wolfpack QB to take over at the end of the season. NC State fired Dave Doeren after a 3-4 start to the season that included a disastrous loss to Vanderbilt.

Rivers, 44, doesn't have any collegiate coaching experience and is currently the head coach at St. Michael Catholic High School in Alabama. His son, Gunner Rivers, is St. Michael's QB. Gunner Rivers is a longtime NC State commit and a four-star prospect in the class of 2027.

NC State is now 4-5 after a loss to Duke in Week 10. The Wolfpack need to win two of their final three games of the season under interim coach Todd Goebbel to make a bowl game.

Doeren had been NC State's coach since 2013 and led the school to eight seasons of eight wins or more. The Wolfpack were 8-5 in 2025, but lost back-to-back games to Wake Forest and Stanford before Doeren was fired. In Week 3, QB CJ Bailey fumbled in the NC State end zone while trying to run out the clock to secure a win. Vanderbilt recovered the ball and won 35-31.

Rivers was a four-year QB at NC State from 2000-2003 before he was the No. 4 pick in the 2004 NFL Draft. Rivers was taken by the Giants and traded to the Chargers as Eli Manning didn't want to play for San Diego.

Before he was drafted, Rivers was the 2003 ACC player of the year and was seventh in the Heisman voting that season.

Rivers played 16 seasons with the Chargers before playing his final full season with the Indianapolis Colts in 2020. He was out of the league for four seasons until the Colts signed him near the end of the 2025 season because of Daniel Jones' Achilles injury. Rivers started three games as the Colts attempted to make the playoffs, but Indianapolis lost all three and missed the postseason.
